# GEO report: harbor-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. All results below are read from code. No live check was run.

## Code score: 40/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.33 ÷ 25 × 100 = 65. High = (16.33 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 65. A blocker applies, so the score is capped at 40. The blocker is GEO-009: `OAI-SearchBot` and `PerplexityBot` are blocked from the whole site.

The pages render well and the basics are in place. Two AI search crawlers are shut out, and both structured-data blocks are broken. Canonicals all point at the home page. The cap assumes you want AI search tools to find the site, because there is no `geo.config.json`. If the blocks are deliberate, tell me and GEO-009 changes.

Routes sampled: `/`, `/moorings`, `/contact`. That is all the routes.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Let the AI search crawlers in
- **Why it matters:** `OAI-SearchBot` (ChatGPT search) and `PerplexityBot` are told to stay away from every page, so those tools can't read the site.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4-8`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: OAI-SearchBot` / `Disallow: /` (and the same for `PerplexityBot`)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 77/100. The cap lifts and GEO-009 earns its 3 points.

### 2. Repair the two broken structured-data blocks
- **Why it matters:** structured data (JSON-LD) labels what a page is. Broken labels get ignored.
- **Where:** `src/data/faq.json:8` and `src/pages/moorings.astro:9`
- **What the code says:** `" ": {` (the key should be `acceptedAnswer`), and `"headline": "Moorings and prices", }` (a trailing comma makes the JSON invalid). The `Article` block also has no `author` or `datePublished`.
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 40 while the cap stays. Without the cap it would be 73. With items 1 and 2 together it is 85.

### 3. Give each page its own canonical
- **Why it matters:** a canonical link names a page's main address. Yours says "the home page" on every page, so search engines are told `/moorings` and `/contact` are duplicates of `/`.
- **Where:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:8`
- **What the code says:** `<link rel="canonical" href="https://harbor.example/" />`
- **Size:** Small. Build the URL from `Astro.url.pathname` and a declared `site` origin.
- **Score after this:** 40 while the cap stays. Without the cap it would be 71. With all three items it is 91.

## Other problems found

- **A noindex page is in the sitemap and the menu.** `public/sitemap.xml:5` has `<loc>https://harbor.example/contact</loc>`, while `src/pages/contact.astro:4` has `robots="noindex"`. Either remove the noindex or take the page out of the sitemap.
- **Every page says `max-snippet:0` by default.** `src/layouts/Base.astro:9` has `content={robots ?? "max-snippet:0"}`. This stops search tools quoting `/` and `/moorings`. Delete the default, or use `index, follow`.

## Worth considering

- **The FAQ is only in JSON-LD, not on the page:** `src/pages/index.astro:8`: `<script type="application/ld+json" set:html={JSON.stringify(faq)}>`. Visitors never see "Can I book by the night?". Showing the questions and answers as page text would help readers, and the markup would then match visible content.
- **The page promises booking but gives no way to book:** `src/pages/index.astro:5`: `description="Book a mooring in Falmouth harbour."`. The page has no booking link or instructions. Say how to book.
- **Prices and contact details could be labelled:** `src/pages/moorings.astro:7` has `Prices start at £40 a night.` and `src/pages/contact.astro:6` has `01326 000000`. Structured data such as `LocalBusiness` or `Offer` might help machines read them.
- **The home page and `/moorings` overlap:** the home page is about moorings and `/moorings` is "Moorings and prices". The home page has no link onward to the prices page except the nav. Add a sentence on the home page that links to `/moorings`.
- **Spelling is inconsistent:** `src/pages/index.astro:5` has `title="Harbor moorings in Cornwall"` while the body says `harbour`. Pick one spelling so the page matches what people search for.
- **Head basics are missing:** `src/layouts/Base.astro:5-10` has no `charset` or `viewport` meta, and the body has no `<main>`. Adding these helps how pages are read.
- **The site URL isn't declared:** there is no `astro.config.*`, so no `site` is set. Setting `site: "https://harbor.example"` would let canonicals and sitemaps be generated from one source.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. If you have an access log, `geopilot logs <access log>` checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Server answers:** the real status codes, redirects and any `X-Robots-Tag` headers need a live check.
- **Training crawlers:** `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` aren't mentioned in `robots.txt`. That's a separate choice and isn't scored.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site, because there is no `geo.config.json`.
- `https://harbor.example` is the intended site origin.
- Noindex on `/contact` may have been deliberate. I flagged the mismatch with the sitemap, not the choice itself.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
